newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Head of EU team to Albania has UN, OSCE experience.
newsitem.headline: Head of EU team to Albania has UN, OSCE experience.

text.p: A Dutch aristocrat heading a high-level European Union mission to Albania this week is a lifelong career diplomat who was previously deputy head of the Netherlands' mission to the United Nations in New York.

Count Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, 55, was due to arrive in Tirana on Monday as head of a team which will discuss how EU military and police experts can help restore order in the anarchic Balkan state.
European Union foreign ministers on Sunday shied away from sending troops to Albania, deciding instead to offer military and police expertise in a strictly advisory capacity.
The Dutch foreign ministry said De Marchant had spent his entire career in the diplomatic service where he currently holds the post of roving ambassador for special missions.
In that capacity he liaised with the U.N. during the aftermath of the Bosnian Serbs' capture of the Moslem enclave of Srebrenica in 1995 while protected by Dutch U.N. peacekeepers.

In a report to Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo he concluded that there was little appetite within the U.N. for a full-blown investigation of the episode in which Bosnian Serb troops alleged to have slaughtered thousands of unarmed Moslem men.

From 1986 to 1989 De Marchant was part of his country's delegation to the conference which led to the creation of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) which is also involved in diplomatic efforts to stabilise Albania.

After a brief spell back in the Netherlands, he served at the Dutch mission to the United Nations from 1990 to 1994, returning to The Hague to head the Foreign Ministry section responsible for bilateral ties with other European countries.
